title: Customer Prioritization Matrix for On‑Prem Requests: Network Windows & Airwall Constraints
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary: We need a repeatable, transparent prioritization matrix specifically for Private/VPC/on‑prem customer requests that involve constrained networking (restricted egress, proxy-only flows), upgrade window restrictions, and airwall/air‑gap-like environments. Current intake is ad‑hoc: PMs and Solutions Engineers manually score tickets, causing inconsistent commitments and missed expectations. This ticket captures the work to define a scoring model, intake template, and a lightweight gating checklist for Sales/SEs to use when triaging new non-bug customer requests (networking, upgrade scheduling, airwall constraints).

Goals: 1) Reduce decision latency for intake from >7 business days to <=48 hours for initial prioritization. 2) Provide reproducible, documented decisions with clear owner and next steps. 3) Surface technical risk buckets to eng and security earlier (networking complexity, required kernel changes, offline upgrade process). 4) Produce a small set of canned offerings (fast-path / standard / custom) and associated SLA/price guidelines.

Scope: - Non-bug customer requests for Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments only. - Networking constraints (proxy-only, restricted CIDR ranges, egress gateways), scheduled upgrade window limits (maintenance windows, blackout periods), and airwall/air‑gap constraints (no outbound connectivity, removable media workflows).

Out of scope: - Hosted API feature requests, dedicated quota increases, or feature parity work unrelated to networking/upgrade constraints.

Work items: - Interview 8 recent enterprise request owners (SE + PM notes) to capture common patterns and failure modes. - Analyze top 20 intake tickets from last 18 months for time-to-ship, unblock reasons, and cost estimates. - Draft a 10‑point scoring rubric (Business impact, Regulatory requirement, Network complexity, Data residency, Upgrade window strictness, Automation feasibility, Security approval lead-time, Customer willingness to pay, Internal implementation effort, Strategic alignment). Each category uses 1–5 scale and weighted sum. - Create an intake form template for Sales/SEs (Confluence + HubSpot/CRM snippet). - Implement a lightweight UI in the PM intake dashboard (product backlog ticket) to record scores and auto-suggest fast-path vs custom. - Ship playbook with example decision outcomes and templated SOW/engagement steps.

Success criteria: - 90% of new qualifying requests scored within 48 hours. - Stakeholder (SE/AE/PM) satisfaction score >=4/5 in post-triage survey. - Reduction in scope creep for on‑site/custom changes by 30% in first quarter post-launch.

Notes & constraints: - Security review is required for airwall cases; coordinate with Security to pre-approve a standard checklist to avoid per-deal delays. - Some customers (regulated FIN/HC) will require longer lead times; the rubric should surface these as "High regulatory" and auto-route to enterprise onboarding. - Pricing guidance must be conservative; engineering-level T-shirt estimates should be attached to scoring ranges to prevent undercommitment.

Artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/OnPrem+Prioritization+Matrix (draft), Example intake form: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleForm, Prior ticket analysis spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExampleSheet, Frontend backlog PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1584 (early UI stub).
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after weekly GTM/SE sync — priority set after three inbound enterprise asks last sprint. Requested preliminary analysis by 2025-02-17.

2025-02-12 Marcus Lee (Solutions Eng): Pulled 18 tickets from Zendesk/Linear for analysis; initial pattern: 55% requests failed due to constrained egress policies, 30% due to no-maintenance windows; adding examples to spreadsheet.
2025-02-13 Lena Novak: Drafted scoring rubric and weights; posted to Confluence. Asked Security (Jamal Thompson) to review rapid-checklist items needed for airwall cases.

2025-02-14 Jamal Thompson (Security): Flagged two items for required KMS/HSM review and a separate audit log retention policy for airwall customers. Q: do we require full HSM or can we accept customer-managed KMS in certain patterns?
2025-02-15 Design review (Elena Park): Recommended intake form changes — prefer radio choices with help text, and a required "expected upgrade cadence" field to clarify maintenance constraints.
2025-02-16 Product leadership (CPO office): Approved rubric in principle; requested a conservative pricing band and a 'fast-path' offering definition for low-risk requests.

2025-02-17 ENG feedback (SRE): Raised dependency ENG-2134 (upgrade orchestration work) — cannot promise <24h turnaround for any request requiring orchestration changes until ENG-2134 ships. Marked as blocker for fast-path automation.
2025-02-18 Lena Novak: Updated playbook to include SE communication templates and next-step owners. Set due date 2025-03-01 for playbook publication and rollout to Sales/SEs.
decision: Adopt weighted scoring rubric (weights: Regulatory 20%, Network complexity 20%, Business impact 20%, Upgrade window strictness 15%, Implementation effort 15%, Willingness-to-pay 10%). Fast-path = score <= 40 and no security blockers; Standard = score 41-70; Custom = score > 70 or any redline security item. Fast-path will have a 10-business-day SLA, Standard 30-business-day baseline, Custom estimated SOW and negotiated timeline.
next_steps: Finalize rubric and publish Confluence playbook (owner: Lena)
Ship intake form snippet to HubSpot (owner: Growth Ops)
Create PM backlog ticket for UI recording scores (owner: Product Eng)
Sync with Security to pre-authorize airwall checklist (owner: Security)
